name: Registry::search_history

test_list.description: A 3-character substring in the middle of a word finds the message through the trigram index.
Queries of one or two characters (below the trigram minimum) still find matches via LIKE.
A query containing double quotes matches the literal text and does not raise an FTS5 syntax error.
Queries such as `foo OR *`, `NEAR(`, `a AND b` and `col:x` match only literal text, never act as FTS5 syntax.
A short query of % or _ matches only messages that contain that character.
At most `limit` hits are returned; limit 0 returns nothing; an absurd limit is capped.
Hits are ordered by message time descending.
An empty query returns an empty list rather than an error or every row.
The hit snippet is bounded in length and contains the matched text for long messages.
Unicode lowercase expansion keeps the snippet offset mapped to source characters, so the matched text remains in the window.
A query above the explicit byte bound returns BadValue before copying it to the bounded database-thread channel.
Both FTS and LIKE paths filter by session in SQL before newest-first ordering and limit.
proptest: text indexed is returned for every substring of 3 or more characters (trigram property).
proptest: search_history on arbitrary bounded query strings (quotes, operators, NUL, unicode) never returns an error.

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: Untrusted user text, matched as a literal substring.

inputs.name: session
inputs.description: Optional session predicate applied in SQL before limiting results.

output_description: Newest-first hits with a bounded snippet.
